34fbca3d-ebe2-4c83-b07f-4c9336e16eff.alternatives: A local HTTP or WebSocket bridge between Studio and the MCP server (a port to manage, impossible from a browser tab without a server). Storing the selection in a model file (would make every click a model change and a git diff). An MCP resource instead of a tool (agents call tools on their own, resources need an explicit mention).
34fbca3d-ebe2-4c83-b07f-4c9336e16eff.consequences: Works in Electron and the browser with no new channel or port. The file is outside the model paths, so it never trips folder-session conflicts or the outside-edit watcher. A selection can be stale when Studio closes without switching models; get_selection reports updatedAt and secondsAgo. Two Studio windows on one folder: the last selection wins.
34fbca3d-ebe2-4c83-b07f-4c9336e16eff.context: People select an element on Studio's canvas and ask a coding agent to change it ("fix the selected mockup"). The MCP server is a separate local process bound to the same model folder; Studio runs in Electron or in a browser with File System Access, so there is no shared process or socket between them.
34fbca3d-ebe2-4c83-b07f-4c9336e16eff.decision: Studio writes the canvas selection (view on screen, selected node and relation ids, time) to .radical/selection.json in the open model folder, debounced, and an empty selection when the user leaves the model. .radical/ carries its own .gitignore. The MCP server's read-only get_selection tool reads it and resolves the ids against the model.
34fbca3d-ebe2-4c83-b07f-4c9336e16eff.label: Canvas selection in model folder

4a69aff2-fb2e-42b8-94c0-cd3134f81855.alternatives: Upgrade Vite: a major upgrade for one bug, with no sign that its lexer has the fix. Turn off identifier minification: a larger bundle. Rename `of` after minification in a plugin: a scope-aware rewrite of a 2.8 MB chunk.
4a69aff2-fb2e-42b8-94c0-cd3134f81855.consequences: The web build takes about 20 s instead of 6 s; the bundle size stays within 1%. terser is a devDependency of Studio.
4a69aff2-fb2e-42b8-94c0-cd3134f81855.context: Vite 5.4 scans every built chunk with the es-module-lexer bundled in it. That lexer reads a variable named `of` inside a for (…) header as the for…of keyword, takes the next `/` for a regular expression and fails the build with "Parse error @:1:1". esbuild's minifier hands out `of` like any short name, so any change that shifts how names are allocated can break the build: adding the state machine types did, inside the bundled ELK code. es-module-lexer 3 fixes it, but Vite 5 ships its own copy.
4a69aff2-fb2e-42b8-94c0-cd3134f81855.decision: Studio's web build and its Electron renderer minify with terser and never use `of` as a name (apps/studio/rendererMinify.ts). Drop this once Vite bundles a fixed lexer.
4a69aff2-fb2e-42b8-94c0-cd3134f81855.label: Terser minifies Studio

5dca88c1-d0f4-400d-85bc-c2cca4402f0b.alternatives: Snap after Smart Layout only (candidates ranked without the rule, so the winner may be a poor fit once snapped); hold alignments only in the live physics (large diagrams, the MCP server and presentations have no physics); constrain only siblings (simpler, but rows across containers are a common ask).
5dca88c1-d0f4-400d-85bc-c2cca4402f0b.consequences: Smart Layout's output for a canvas without constraints stays identical. Alignments centre on the size the canvas draws (drawnSize), not the stored size the engines place. New constraint kinds (spacing, fixed position) extend the same type and both solvers.
5dca88c1-d0f4-400d-85bc-c2cca4402f0b.context: Users want some elements to stay in a row or a column on a canvas whatever moves. "Graph views use Smart Layout" says Smart Layout's positions are not post-processed, and the live WebCoLa physics, Smart Layout and the MCP server each place nodes.
5dca88c1-d0f4-400d-85bc-c2cca4402f0b.decision: A canvas (a view, or All elements) keeps layout constraints (LayoutConstraint): 'align' (equal centre x or y, optionally keeping the members' order along the line), 'grid' (cells filled row by row, expanded into ordered rows and columns that keep their rank) and 'pin' (see "Calm drags pin what they drop"). Every engine honours the alignments and grids: WebCoLa holds an alignment of leaves with its own alignment constraint and an order with separation constraints, and one with an expanded container by a projection after each tick; Smart Layout applies enforceAlignments (@radical/layout constraints.ts) inside its finalisation, so every candidate is ranked and refined with the alignment applied; the store and the MCP server apply the same pass after their parent refit. This is the one post-processing of Smart Layout's positions allowed, and it changes nothing when a canvas has no constraints.
5dca88c1-d0f4-400d-85bc-c2cca4402f0b.label: User alignments bind layout

6f2e9a6a-ab1c-4773-9904-15ec6348a193.consequences: Studio shows edits made by the MCP server or an editor on the open canvas. A writer re-reads after a refused write. Amended 2026-10-14 (exploratory run 6): a JSON file of the folder that is there but does not parse (a trailing comma, git conflict markers, a file caught half written) is an error that names the file (MalformedFolderFileError in deserializeFromMdFolder), not a missing file. It used to read as empty: Studio showed the model without its relations, views or layout and removed the file as stale on the next save. Studio now tells the user which file it is, keeps the model that was on screen when the file broke while the folder was open, and refuses every save to that folder until a read succeeds (DocumentUnreadableError in the document store); the folder is still watched, so the fix arrives as an outside edit. The MCP server already refused such a folder. Amended again 2026-10-14 (runs 9 and 12): a node .md file with git conflict markers is the same error (it was skipped as no node, and the next save dropped its layout); front matter keys that are not letters, digits, _ or - are written JSON-quoted and read back (a property keyed "SLA target" was lost); a node the layout file does not know gets its type's size instead of 0x0.
6f2e9a6a-ab1c-4773-9904-15ec6348a193.context: People edit model files in other editors and through git while Studio or the MCP server has the folder open. Earlier versions lost descriptions, deleted foreign files and overwrote outside edits.
6f2e9a6a-ab1c-4773-9904-15ec6348a193.decision: MdFolderSession keeps a baseline of what it read, refuses a write when a file changed outside since then, and polls the folder for outside edits.
6f2e9a6a-ab1c-4773-9904-15ec6348a193.label: Folder writes refuse conflicts

742c9ca4-1e99-4c0b-8e5b-2c6dd667dccf.alternatives: A socket or HTTP bridge between Studio and the server (a port to manage, impossible from a browser tab). The run's state in a model file (every step would be a model change and a git diff). MCP notifications (they reach the agent's client, not Studio). Answering the agent's questions from Studio (a channel back and a rule for who wins; left for later).
742c9ca4-1e99-4c0b-8e5b-2c6dd667dccf.consequences: People see an agent's Forge run where they look at the model, without switching to the agent's window. The file is outside the model paths, so it never trips the folder session or the outside-edit watcher, and .radical/.gitignore keeps it out of git. Two servers on one folder overwrite each other's status. A killed server cannot close its run, so Studio shows it until the 30 minutes pass. Studio reads the file every 2 s for a folder model even when no agent is connected.
742c9ca4-1e99-4c0b-8e5b-2c6dd667dccf.context: An agent can run Radical Forge over MCP (ADR Forge on the agent's model), but Studio, open on the same folder, saw only elements appearing, not which stage the run was at or that the agent was waiting for an answer in its chat. The MCP server and Studio share no process or socket, only the model folder (as for ADR Canvas selection in model folder), and the server keeps the run in memory.
742c9ca4-1e99-4c0b-8e5b-2c6dd667dccf.decision: After every forge_* step that succeeds, the MCP server writes the run's status to .radical/forge-run.json in the model folder (@radical/common formats/forgeRunStatus.ts, @radical/node-files): the client's name, the need, each stage's status (pending, clarifying, generating, done with summary and counts) and active / finished / closed; it marks an unfinished run closed when its client goes away. Studio polls the file every 2 s for the open md-folder model (Electron through IPC, the browser through the folder handle). The Forge button in the search bar pulses blue while a stage is generated and amber while the agent waits for the user, shows the stage it is at, and opens a read-only view with the wizard's step bar and one line of status; it stops when the run finishes, closes, or goes 30 minutes without a change. Studio never writes to the run.
742c9ca4-1e99-4c0b-8e5b-2c6dd667dccf.label: Agent Forge runs show in Studio

7771ef8d-79c8-4dc8-820c-a83203747cd3.alternatives: After the scenarios, next to the state machines (the scenarios would invent their own nouns first). Inside the C4 stage (domains would follow the decomposition instead of shaping it). Entities nested in their aggregate root by containment (an aggregate's parts would hide inside a card, and containment cannot express references). The domain model only in the Domain view (the owner wants it in Conceptual for now).
7771ef8d-79c8-4dc8-820c-a83203747cd3.consequences: One language runs through a run, and the State machines and C4 stages link to elements that already exist instead of creating duplicates. A run has seven stages; the wizard's step bar fits nine steps on one line only with short labels (Fitness, C4) and tight pills. The domain model shows twice (Domain and Conceptual) until Conceptual drops it. Entities have no attributes or value objects yet.
7771ef8d-79c8-4dc8-820c-a83203747cd3.context: Each Radical Forge stage named things its own way: scenarios, state machines and C4 each made up the nouns of the system, and the State machines stage created entities of its own. The metamodel had domains and entities but no relations between entities, and no stage built a domain model, although DDD's ubiquitous language is what the later stages should share.
7771ef8d-79c8-4dc8-820c-a83203747cd3.decision: A Domain model stage runs right after Requirements and before Fitness functions: Requirements → Domain model → Fitness functions → Gherkin scenarios → State machines → Mockups → C4 model. It adds `domain` nodes (bounded contexts, kind core/supporting/generic) holding `entity` nodes in the requirements' words, groups entities into aggregates with a new `part-of` relation (entity → aggregate root), links aggregates with a new `references` relation (entity → entity, cardinality one or many), maps the domains with `depends-on` and `partnership`, and links each entity to its requirements with `satisfies`. Later stages use it: scenarios name its entities, the State machines stage takes its entities (adding one only when missing), and C4 adds `realises` to domains and entities. Its output goes into a new Domain view and, at the owner's request, also into Conceptual; a type may now go into several Forge views. @radical/common's domainModel.ts warns about entities outside any aggregate, parts of two aggregates, parts of a non-root and roots inside another aggregate.
7771ef8d-79c8-4dc8-820c-a83203747cd3.label: Forge models the domain first

I want to describe a system in a few plain-language paragraphs and get a first model out of it: requirements, quality guardrails, test scenarios, the screens users will see and a C4 structure. I don't want one opaque answer, though; I want to review and steer each step before the next one builds on it, and stop when I have enough.

845b36fd-6167-46a8-9d47-4081bf588b16.alternatives: Requirements inside the radical.tools system: needs a metamodel change and buries the containers under about 400 records. Separate Requirements and Decisions groups next to the system: tidier, but keeps the layers implicit. Separate logical and physical layers (tried on 2026-10-06 and merged the same day): C4 already mixes the two, so the line was arbitrary and the physical layer held only the shared packages, which belong inside the system (ADR Groups inside a system). DDD domains per product area linked with realises: the areas are product features rather than bounded contexts.
845b36fd-6167-46a8-9d47-4081bf588b16.consequences: The Structure view shows three frames, and the satisfies relations carry the trace from requirements to the parts that meet them. Every named view also shows its layer's frame, because views include all ancestors of their nodes. C4 is both logical and physical (containers name their technology, packages are code), so the model does not split the two.
845b36fd-6167-46a8-9d47-4081bf588b16.context: The root of architecture/ held 35 elements side by side: the radical.tools system, six requirement groups, a loose need and five loose requirements, nine ADRs, five fitness functions, the people, the external systems and the shared packages. Requirements cannot simply move into the system: the metamodel does not allow a group inside a system, and a C4 system boundary holds what runs, not what is asked of it. The shared packages are code of radical.tools, but a component cannot sit directly in a system either.
845b36fd-6167-46a8-9d47-4081bf588b16.decision: The root holds three groups and nothing else. 1 Conceptual: what the product must do and why (needs, EARS requirements and scenarios, one group per product area, plus Product principles for the cross-cutting ones). 2 Logical & physical: what it is made of and how it is built, in C4 (people, external systems, and the radical.tools system with its containers, components and shared packages; deployment nodes once the C4 preset has a type for them). Decisions: ADRs and fitness functions, beside the layers because they cut across them. A new element goes into the layer it describes. Layers are linked by relations (satisfies, derives, verifies, constrains, traces-to), never by containment.
845b36fd-6167-46a8-9d47-4081bf588b16.label: Model in two layers

8a2fb157-4bb6-4043-9748-42152f8cb625.consequences: A new tool needs a facade method in both facades (Studio's store and the headless createModelFacade); the facade parity test proves they behave the same. Amended 2026-10-14 after exploratory runs 13 to 24: the handlers check element and relation types against the metamodel each call runs on (add_node and update_node refuse an unknown type). The MCP server still lists the types in its tool schemas, but checks a call against the schema without those lists: the SDK validated calls against the metamodel the server had seen last, so a type that Studio, another server or a hand edit had just added was refused until another call refreshed the schemas.
8a2fb157-4bb6-4043-9748-42152f8cb625.context: Studio's AI chat, Radical Forge and the MCP server all edit the model through tools. Separate implementations would drift apart.
8a2fb157-4bb6-4043-9748-42152f8cb625.decision: Define every tool once in @radical/common (src/ai/tools): definition plus handler over a model facade. Studio's chat gets every tool and Forge leaves out the metamodel and presentation groups. The MCP server serves the catalogue without the canvas-only set_active_view and focus_node and the destructive reset_diagram, and adds get_model_summary and smart_layout.
8a2fb157-4bb6-4043-9748-42152f8cb625.label: One AI tool catalogue

8a93c06a-1e5c-4360-b2c6-c16a367ffc97.action: The system shall set its type to the one restricted relation type that allows the source and target pair, and leave it untyped when no type or several types match.

8c66e024-79f9-42d0-86cd-843cefd2a7ef.description: The `radical` command line (apps/cli, package @radicaltools/cli, private until a distribution decision). `radical check [folder]` checks a Markdown model folder before a commit or in CI: the files read as a model, the model follows its metamodel, it is complete (requirements have scenarios, accepted ADRs fitness functions, scenarios and fitness functions name their tests, …), and with --report the tests they name passed in the Vitest, Jest, Playwright or JUnit reports given. --evidence writes the status of each scenario, fitness function, requirement and ADR as JSON, and --report also keeps the test cases in the folder's .radical/test-results.json for Studio's Inspector. It never writes the model's own files. Rules are set per project in check.json in the model folder (or --config), with baselines that --ratchet lowers and writes back. Output as text, JSON or GitHub annotations; exit 0 (no errors), 1 (errors) or 2 (could not run). The rules live in @radical/common (src/check), so Studio's Inspector runs the same check. The build bundles the private workspaces, as the MCP server's does. CI keeps the test reports (artifact test-reports) but does not run radical check, since architecture/ is not in the repository; npm run check:architecture runs it locally.

938c5612-ec43-4d40-bea5-479f2c9f8c14.alternatives: Only editor validation: misses merges, hand edits and metamodel changes, and cannot demand completeness. Only a CI check: users would build invalid models and learn about it in the pull request.
938c5612-ec43-4d40-bea5-479f2c9f8c14.consequences: Something Studio lets a user build and its own validation then flags stays a Studio bug, not a job for the check. The check runs the same validator (validateModel) as Studio's Validation list, with the same severities; a project raises them in its config. Completeness rules are warnings by default and become a gate per project with a baseline that only goes down.
938c5612-ec43-4d40-bea5-479f2c9f8c14.context: Studio and the MCP server already keep the metamodel while a model is edited through them. A model also changes in other ways: hand edits of the Markdown files, a git merge of two valid branches (one deletes an element, the other adds a relation to it), a script, an older Studio, a changed metamodel. And completeness (a requirement without a scenario) is a legal state while someone is still writing, so no editor can refuse it.
938c5612-ec43-4d40-bea5-479f2c9f8c14.decision: Studio and the MCP server prevent what breaks the metamodel at the moment of the edit and say why. `radical check` detects, at the gate: what came in another way, and completeness gaps, which editors only show. Each rule is one of the two kinds, and both kinds live in one catalogue in @radical/common.
938c5612-ec43-4d40-bea5-479f2c9f8c14.label: Editors prevent, check detects

939dde75-a293-4aab-a570-2b2c28ef5011.alternatives: Keep relaxing small diagrams and compute Smart Layout's score and report after the physics has settled (C4 diagrams keep ending with a worse layout than Smart Layout chose). Rest after Smart Layout and on opening but keep relaxing the whole diagram on every edit (the first added element after a layout rearranges everything at once). Run the relaxed candidate in Studio only, with the engine left in @radical/ui (layouts made through the MCP server of models with many root elements come out about twice as wide as in Studio). Give relations to open containers a force inside WebCoLa: a link to the nearest leaf inside the container bends what is inside it, and pulling every related element after each step never comes to rest.
939dde75-a293-4aab-a570-2b2c28ef5011.consequences: The layout Smart Layout reports is the one saved and shown, in Studio and through the MCP server alike, and a model opened again does not change (no drift of a few pixels per load in a folder under git). Smart Layout takes longer on diagrams under 150 nodes (about 2.7 s more on 137 elements). What users see on small C4 diagrams changes: they used to see the physics' arrangement (people above, external systems to the right, by its separation constraints), now the candidate that scores best, which may place them otherwise; the e2e screenshot baselines of laid-out views change with it. A small diagram that arrives without a layout from a file (overlapping elements) is no longer arranged on opening; Studio shows the hint to run Smart Layout that large diagrams already got. On a small diagram, adding a relation, deleting or collapsing an element moves nothing, and an element an agent adds through the MCP server while Studio is open stays where the server put it. Relations that end on an open container still have no force in the physics; an element on the canvas with only such relations is drawn back next to them when the physics runs (holdByGroups), through free room only. Amended 2026-10-13 after exploratory runs 2 and 3: an open container keeps the frame the model has until one of its leaves moves against the others (a drag or an added element elsewhere used to re-frame every open container to the physics' padding); and the physics imposes its C4 order (people above everything else, external systems to the right) only when it arranges a diagram (first start, relaxLayout). On a diagram that has a layout it keeps that order only where the layout has it: imposed there, the first element the physics was free to move was thrown across the diagram (a system dropped after a push drag on a 150-element grid ended up 3 400 px below it). Amended 2026-10-14 after exploratory runs 4 to 6: a collapse moves nothing at any diagram size. A container that is collapsed turns from a frame around others into one box; the engine took that box for a new element and freed the 40 elements nearest to it, which reached into other containers whose frames and other children stayed fixed (in a model nested four levels deep one collapse left 17 to 41 elements moving two minutes later, with containers overlapping). It is no longer counted as new: the container shrinks to the centre of its box and the rest stands. The room it leaves stays until the user lays the canvas out. Each canvas also gives a place of its own to an element added on another canvas (placeUnplaced in @radical/layout: right of the siblings it has placed, ancestors refit, then settled by the physics as a new element is), when the canvas is shown and when a document is loaded; such an element used to keep the other canvas's place, outside its parent's frame. Amended 2026-10-14 after run 11: the relaxed candidate is scored with its containers fitted to their children, as applying it fits them. Scored with the physics' own frames, the winner on the sample's All elements scored better than what was saved, so every later Smart Layout reported an improvement, moved nothing and left an empty undo step. Amended 2026-10-14 after exploratory run 19 (150 to 600 elements): an expand is no longer left to the physics. Every child it showed counted as new and freed the 40 elements nearest to it by relation, in other systems whose frames stayed fixed (215 elements: 93 moved across all five systems, 99 still moving after 60 s, a reload drew another picture). The store now makes room as it does without physics: the children come back where they were, the expanded container's siblings and each ancestor's siblings are separated (separateSiblings), a parent frame grows left or up when a child reaches past it, and the physics takes the result as it is (reset). From 150 nodes up a push drag (Cmd/Ctrl) is a calm drag: freeing the 40 nearest by relation and freezing the rest threw them thousands of pixels toward frozen elements they were related to and left them on top of others. The hint that a diagram is not laid out yet measures elements as drawn (a collapsed container at its collapsed size, what it holds not at all).
939dde75-a293-4aab-a570-2b2c28ef5011.context: On diagrams under 150 nodes the live WebCoLa physics relaxed the whole diagram after every rebuild: on opening a model, on a view switch, an undo, and right after Smart Layout. Measured with Smart Layout's own composite score, raw winner against the same layout after the physics: the sample model's All elements 16 937 to 20 713 (crossings 145 to 223), Core Banking 5 to 47, System Context 0 to 14, every element moved, by up to 1 690 px. What was saved and shown after a reload was the physics' layout, not the one Smart Layout chose and reported. Only a Forge-built model with 76 root elements improved (353 349 to 303 022), because the engines spread it over 10 700 x 12 300. An element related only to open containers was not held by anything and ended up far from the diagram. The MCP server has no physics, so its smart_layout result looked different once Studio opened the folder.
939dde75-a293-4aab-a570-2b2c28ef5011.decision: A diagram that has a layout keeps it. The live physics takes the positions it is given on every rebuild (open, view switch, undo, milestone, Smart Layout) and moves nothing; it moves only nodes that are new since the previous build (added, or shown by an expand) with their nearest surroundings, at every diagram size, as it already did from 150 nodes up. The members of an alignment or grid just made, which the store snaps onto their line, settle the same way: they and their surroundings move, the rest stays. The physics still moves a whole diagram in three cases, all below 150 nodes: to arrange one that has no layout yet (first start), during a push drag (Cmd/Ctrl), which asks for it, and as relaxLayout: the same physics run over a whole diagram in one go, counted in steps, not time. Smart Layout scores relaxLayout of its winner as one more candidate and keeps it only when it scores better than the winner. The engine (LiveColaEngine, relaxLayout) moves from @radical/ui to @radical/layout, which gains webcola, d3-dispatch, d3-timer and d3-drag as dependencies, so the MCP server's smart_layout computes the same candidate; its build bundles them. This amends "Graph views use Smart Layout": no physics pass follows Smart Layout on a model's canvas any more. The metamodel editor's diagram keeps its own pass (relaxLive, animated): it is laid out anew each time it is drawn, and Smart Layout alone spreads its category frames over a mostly empty canvas.
939dde75-a293-4aab-a570-2b2c28ef5011.label: A laid-out diagram stands

984afb23-9553-4ada-aea9-318b97228ce7.description: Amazon Web Services account that hosts the three public sites, defined in infra/ (Terraform, AWS provider, region eu-west-1; local state, terraform.tfvars git-ignored). A Route 53 hosted zone for radical.tools (its name servers set at the registrar, domeny.tv) points the apex and www at the website distribution and studio and hub at theirs; one ACM certificate in us-east-1 covers all four names. iam.tf trusts GitHub's OIDC provider and gives GitHub Actions runs from main of the repository (matched by its immutable repository id) a deploy role that may only put, get, delete and list objects in the three buckets and create CloudFront invalidations; no long-lived AWS keys exist.

a24dc7fb-8ebb-4faa-ba2f-c1989c426867.alternatives: Transitions as nodes with relations to their events: real links, but a statechart stops looking like one, orphaned transitions need cascades, and one transition costs three tool calls. Names as text checked against labels (the first version): a rename breaks the link, and raised events had to be parsed from prose. Relations between relations: a new graph concept for every layout engine, view and file format.
a24dc7fb-8ebb-4faa-ba2f-c1989c426867.consequences: A rename of the target never breaks a reference, and the canvas shows the new name at once. Deleting a node leaves the references to it dangling, with a warning in the metamodel editor's Validation list (and from the MCP server) and a marked entry in the picker, until someone removes them. Ids are unreadable in raw files; Studio and search_model show labels. A property's value can now be an array, which code that assumed scalars has to handle (frontmatter, query language, table cells).
a24dc7fb-8ebb-4faa-ba2f-c1989c426867.context: A transition had to name its trigger and the events it raises. A relation can only connect two nodes, so the first version stored the event's name as text: a rename broke the link silently, and events raised in actions were parsed out of prose (`raise OrderPaid`). Making the transition a node would allow real relations, but turns every arrow into a box and two edges, needs cascades for orphaned transitions, and triples the tool calls agents and Forge make.
a24dc7fb-8ebb-4faa-ba2f-c1989c426867.decision: The metamodel gets a property type 'ref' (packages/common/src/metamodel/refs.ts): `refType` names the node type it points at and `multiple` allows several. The value is the node's id, or an array of ids; files keep it as such (relations.json, and a one-line JSON array in a node's frontmatter). validateModel warns about an id with no node or a node of another type. The AI tools accept ids or tempIds from the same run and refuse a node of the wrong type; the metamodel context tells agents so, and upsert_node_type and the metamodel editor define such properties. Studio picks references with one component (RefPicker: a list, or chips to add and remove) in the properties panel, the table, the wiki and the node wizard, and shows the nodes' labels. search_model matches a list when one of its ids does. Transitions use it: `event` (one) and `raises` (several) point at event nodes.
a24dc7fb-8ebb-4faa-ba2f-c1989c426867.label: Properties can reference nodes

a4fd393a-bafe-4c7e-a795-4c93e467e60a.alternatives: Model the shared packages as a container: wrong in C4, since a container is something that runs or stores data. Allow the group only in this model's metamodel: editing a built-in preset forks it, so the model would stop getting preset updates (ADR Edited presets fork). Groups inside containers as well: not needed yet, and nested groups inside a container change how the canvas fits and lays out components.
a4fd393a-bafe-4c7e-a795-4c93e467e60a.consequences: Every model on a built-in preset gets the rule on its next load, since presets refresh on load; nothing in an existing model becomes invalid. The metamodel diagram draws one more Contains edge (System → Group), and the e2e counts were raised to match. A system can now hold parts that are not C4 containers, which is a convention, not a C4 level.
a4fd393a-bafe-4c7e-a795-4c93e467e60a.context: The shared packages are code of radical.tools, so in its own model they belong inside the radical.tools system. They are components, which may sit in a container, web app or group but not directly in a system, and the C4 preset allowed a group only at the root or in another group. The model had to keep them in a group outside the system. Structurizr allows groups inside a software system for the same purpose.
a4fd393a-bafe-4c7e-a795-4c93e467e60a.decision: The C4 preset, which the C4, C4 + DDD and governance presets share, allows a group inside a system (packages/common/src/metamodel/presets/c4.ts). Groups still cannot sit inside a container, web app or component.

ae71db46-0614-4310-95b7-6d6ed8f54a52.alternatives: Test ids as tags in the test code (`@REQ-12`): ties every test file to the model's ids and puts them in a second place. Writing the status into the model's files: every CI run would change files in git. Gherkin feature files run by Cucumber: the repository's tests are plain Vitest and Playwright, and rewriting them is out of proportion.
ae71db46-0614-4310-95b7-6d6ed8f54a52.consequences: A renamed or deleted test fails the check (test-not-found) in the run that would have run it, and a failing test names the requirements or ADRs it leaves unverified. Test reports from runners other than JavaScript ones work through JUnit XML. Matching by title means a renamed test needs its id updated in the model too. Each CI run can produce evidence without a commit to the model. A check that is no test runner (a script such as test-package.mjs, tools/check-workspaces.mjs, a benchmark) cannot be named yet.
ae71db46-0614-4310-95b7-6d6ed8f54a52.context: 117 scenarios named their tests in a `# Covered by:` comment in the gherkin field and the fitness functions in prose in their descriptions. Nothing could tell when such a test was renamed or deleted: the first check of them against real reports found four stale bindings (two titles cut short, one test moved to another file, one test gone since #176). Requirements and ADRs had no status a person or an agent could read.
ae71db46-0614-4310-95b7-6d6ed8f54a52.decision: Scenarios and fitness functions have a `tests` property: one test id per line, `<file> › <title>` as Vitest and Playwright print them. An id names the test whose title it ends, else every test in the describe block it starts; an id without a title names every test in the file or directory. `radical check --report` reads Vitest/Jest JSON, Playwright JSON and JUnit XML reports and looks the ids up; with --evidence it writes the status of each scenario, fitness function, requirement and ADR to a JSON file. The evidence never goes into the model's files.
ae71db46-0614-4310-95b7-6d6ed8f54a52.label: The model names its tests

b9eb64d3-73a7-4fb4-929b-38317f58956e.alternatives: The full UML notation (regions, entry and exit points, junctions and forks as their own types): more types without more meaning for what people, agents and Forge write. A region type: a parallel state's children are regions already. Pseudostates as kinds of state: a pseudostate is never active, holds nothing and has a fixed small size, which the metamodel ties to the type. A machine tied straight to a C4 element (the first draft, `lifecycle-of` machine → component): it mixed what the lifecycle is of with what runs it. The entity as text on the machine (`subject`, the first draft): nothing to link requirements, owners or other machines to. Transitions as nodes linked to their events: see ADR Properties can reference nodes. A separate behaviour preset: models on the governance preset would not get it, and presets extend each other.
b9eb64d3-73a7-4fb4-929b-38317f58956e.consequences: Every model on the unedited governance preset gets the types on its next load (ADR Edited presets fork). The palette and the metamodel diagram have a States group; unit and e2e counts were raised to match. Radical Forge got a State machines stage between the scenarios and the mockups, with a States view of its own (ADR Forge files its output into layer views), and the MCP server returns the statechart warnings a write brings in. Statecharts are laid out by the general Smart Layout, which knows nothing of their cycles and long labels yet; a layered layout for them is the next step.
b9eb64d3-73a7-4fb4-929b-38317f58956e.context: The product owner asked for event-driven hierarchical state machines in the metamodel, and for a Radical Forge stage that derives them from the scenarios before the mockups. The lifecycle of an entity (an order, a payment) had no notation: Gherkin scenarios describe its state changes, but nothing in the model held the states. The metamodel already has nesting (canvas containment), typed relations with properties and soft validation.
b9eb64d3-73a7-4fb4-929b-38317f58956e.decision: The C4 + DDD + Governance preset gets four node types, state-machine, state, pseudostate and event, with SCXML / XState semantics, and the DDD preset an `entity` type (a domain object; kind aggregate-root or entity). States nest by containment inside a machine or another state; a state with child states is compound; kind parallel makes its child states regions active at once; kind final ends its parent. A machine and every compound state that is not parallel enter through one initial pseudostate with a single transition to the default child. The model keeps three concerns apart: a machine is the lifecycle of one entity (`lifecycle-of`, machine → entity, one machine per entity); the C4 elements that run it implement it (`implements`, system/container/component/web app → machine, extending the relation fitness functions use for ADRs); the element that owns the entity's data realises it (`realises`, C4 → entity, extending the DDD relation). A transition carries guard, actions and kind, and points at its trigger (`event`) and at the events it raises (`raises`) with reference properties (ADR Properties can reference nodes); a state-driven requirement points at the state it holds in with `precondition_state`, and its EARS sentence reads "While the <entity> is <state>". A state publishes an event with emits (on entry, exit or do). @radical/common's statechart.ts checks the statechart rules as warnings in validateModel, including a machine with no entity and an entity with two machines. The canvas draws statechart notation, names a machine after its entity, labels a transition `event [guard] / actions ^raised`, and the live layout nests machines and states like systems, domains and groups.
b9eb64d3-73a7-4fb4-929b-38317f58956e.label: State machines as nested states

ba0d2e93-b48a-49cd-bc41-4f6f522a70f7.alternatives: Keep C4 + DDD loadable as a hidden preset: no change for existing models, but a third metamodel stays in the code. Rename the id too: breaks every saved model and Hub concept, or needs a migration everywhere. Keep governance and c4-ddd as aliases of radical for --metamodel: friendlier to old configurations, but two names for one thing.
ba0d2e93-b48a-49cd-bc41-4f6f522a70f7.consequences: One fewer choice when a model is created, and the default is called what the product is: the picker reads Radical or C4. Models on C4 + DDD gain the governance types on their next load; nothing in them becomes invalid. Edited copies of the default are named "Radical (custom)". An MCP configuration that passes --metamodel governance or c4-ddd stops with the usage message and must switch to radical. Saved files keep the old name text until they are saved again; the loaded name comes from the preset.
ba0d2e93-b48a-49cd-bc41-4f6f522a70f7.context: Studio offered three nested presets, C4, C4 + DDD Domains and C4 + DDD + Governance, with the last as the default. The middle one added only the Domain and Entity types, which the default holds too, so the choice asked people to understand three notations to pick one, and the default had a name that described its history rather than the product. The product owner asked for two: the default under the product's name, and plain C4.
ba0d2e93-b48a-49cd-bc41-4f6f522a70f7.decision: Two built-in metamodels: Radical (the former C4 + DDD + Governance, the default) and C4. Radical keeps the id c4-ddd-governance-builtin, since files, folders and 128 Hub concepts store it; only its name changes (RADICAL_METAMODEL_NAME = "Radical"). C4 + DDD leaves the pickers; its builder stays as the base Radical extends, and a document saved with its id loads under Radical. The MCP server's --metamodel takes radical or c4 (default radical); the old values c4-ddd and governance are refused.
ba0d2e93-b48a-49cd-bc41-4f6f522a70f7.label: Two built-in metamodels

bf6fefab-84b5-42d6-b80c-035097128389.description:
Checked by hand around layout changes, not in CI. The score is computeCompositeScore in packages/layout/src/smartLayout.ts (rendered crossings, overdraws, stub loops, overlap, edge lengths, leaf centrality, aspect ratio, compactness, symmetry and label crowding, weighted in scoreWeights.ts); computeLayoutMetrics in packages/layout/src/crossingOpt.ts gives the straight-line crossings and overdraws. packages/layout/tests/saThroughput.bench.mjs runs runSmartLayoutCore five times on a 20-element fintech-like diagram and prints wall time, annealing iterations and iterations per second, composite and rendered crossings. packages/layout/tests/visual/layoutHarness.mjs lays out four scenarios (screenshot, chain, hub, microservices), prints their score terms and writes tests/visual/out-<name>.svg. Both run with node --import tsx from packages/layout (tsx is not a dependency of @radical/layout; it resolves from other workspaces). Results are deterministic for a given diagram: the annealing is seeded from the graph structure (graphSeed) and its budgets are counted in work, and the wall-clock deadlines (3 s, 1.5 s, 1.5 s) only cut pathological inputs; repeated runs give the same composite, so compare several fixtures at several seeds (runSmartLayoutCore options.seed, at least five) instead of repeated runs. packages/layout/tests/smartLayoutScoring.test.mjs, part of npm test, checks that the score ranks a hand-fixed layout better than the algorithm's.

Threshold: No drop in the composite score, averaged over the fixtures at five or more seeds, against main. Pure refactors keep runSmartLayoutCore's output identical over the fixture set (the fintech sample plus the Hub blueprints and patterns), proved by hashing the full result; that hashing script is not in the repo.

cf57028b-d044-4957-9f74-03af8bead446.alternatives: `radical lint`: a lint is static and fast and has --fix, while the check will also read test results and judge whether the system works. A separate radical-check executable per command: one name per tool to install and document. Putting the check into the MCP server: a pipeline cannot use a stdio server, and the server's package version is its MCP handshake version.
cf57028b-d044-4957-9f74-03af8bead446.consequences: A new app depends only on packages (Monorepo with npm workspaces). Studio's Validation list, get_issues and a future MCP tool can show the same findings as CI. A pipeline needs the model folder in the repository; this repository's own architecture/ is local-only, so its CI runs the command's tests, not a check of the model.
cf57028b-d044-4957-9f74-03af8bead446.context: Checking a model in CI (files, metamodel, completeness, later test evidence and code drift) needs a command a pipeline can run. The only executable so far is radical-mcp, an MCP server over stdio, which a CI job cannot use as a check. More commands will follow (headless Smart Layout, export and import).
cf57028b-d044-4957-9f74-03af8bead446.decision: Add one `radical` executable in a new app, apps/cli (@radicaltools/cli), with subcommands; the first is `radical check`. The command line only reads files, formats and sets the exit status: the rules live in @radical/common (src/check) and are pure functions of the folder's files and a config. The MCP server keeps its radical-mcp executable; serving it as `radical mcp` too is a later step. The package stays private until it is published the way Public MCP distribution publishes the MCP server.
cf57028b-d044-4957-9f74-03af8bead446.label: One radical CLI

d3ee2fc1-24f6-4646-af5f-7b98157ce4aa.description: packages/layout: Smart Layout and the other headless layout engines, used by Studio and bundled into the MCP server. smartLayout.ts: the ensemble of ten engines (elkLayout.ts: five ELK layered variants, a metamodel-aware layered layout, stress, force, Mr.Tree; radicalLayout.ts: semantic C4), crossing minimisation by sibling swaps (crossingOpt.ts), the render-aware composite score (weights in scoreWeights.ts), simulated annealing in three phases (annealing.ts), finalisation that separates siblings and fits containers (layoutFinalize.ts) with room for relation labels (labelRoom.ts), and the relaxed winner as a last candidate. elkLayout.ts also has the hierarchical tree layout (applyTreeLayout). constraints.ts resolves and enforces row, column and grid alignments; viewInput.ts gives what a layout of one view sees and writes its result back (shared by Studio's store and the MCP server); geometry.ts places new and imported elements (placeNewNode, freeSpotNear, createBatchPlacer, placeUnplaced). For the canvas: edgeRouting.ts (Bezier edges, A* routing around elements), portAllocator.ts (sides and spread connection points) and edgeLabels.ts (label sizes and placement). liveColaEngine.ts: the live WebCoLa physics (LiveColaEngine, which the canvas runs in a worker; calm and push drags, pins, alignments, holdByGroups) and relaxLayout, which Smart Layout scores as a candidate. The product's core IP.
d3ee2fc1-24f6-4646-af5f-7b98157ce4aa.label: @radical/layout

d6498d93-94a3-4abc-b5e5-377fe38e846b.alternatives: Layer groups as in this repo's model (moving elements into containers changes the model, not how it is viewed); one view per stage (requirements and the scenarios that verify them apart); all three views created at the start (an empty view shows the whole model); arranging every stage automatically (the owner asked to be asked, and Smart Layout on a large view takes seconds and redraws what they arranged by hand).
d6498d93-94a3-4abc-b5e5-377fe38e846b.consequences: Each layer is readable on its own and a stage no longer lands on the previous one. Relations across layers (satisfies, traces-to, constrains, verifies from a scenario to a state machine) show on none of the views; All elements and the table views still show everything. The name is the key: a renamed view makes the next run create a new one, and a regenerated stage leaves its view in place (empty, it shows the whole model again). Chat runs in Studio place sideways too. A grid or row the user picks is a layout constraint like any other (ADR User alignments bind layout). State machines get one shared States view rather than one view per machine: a run rarely makes more than three, and their frames keep them apart.
d6498d93-94a3-4abc-b5e5-377fe38e846b.context: Radical Forge put every stage's elements on whatever canvas was open, placed by the AI runner in rows of four that restarted at the same spot each run. A full run (dozens of requirements, scenarios, fitness functions and C4 elements) became one tall canvas whose stages lay on top of each other until the live physics pushed them apart. This repo's own model reads in layers (ADR Model in two layers), and its owner asked for the same split and to be asked how to arrange each stage.
d6498d93-94a3-4abc-b5e5-377fe38e846b.decision: A Forge run adds each element to its static views by type: Conceptual (need, requirement, scenario, mockup), Domain (domain, entity; added 2026-10-09 with the Domain model stage, and for now also in Conceptual), States (state-machine, state, pseudostate, event, plus the entity each new machine is the lifecycle of; added 2026-10-09), Logical & physical (C4 elements) and Governance (fitness-fn, adr); any other type follows its stage. A type may go into several views (forgeViewsOf). A view is found by name and created when its first element arrives, because an empty view shows the whole model. Studio runs a stage on its view (on All elements while the view does not exist yet) and shows the view afterwards; the MCP server files the elements at forge_start and forge_complete_stage and writes their positions on the view. New elements go beside what the canvas shows, in a block that grows wider than tall (landscapeSlot, createBatchPlacer). After each stage Forge asks whether to keep the stage's outermost new elements in a row or a column (in creation order) or a landscape grid on each view, and whether to run Smart Layout on it: Studio's Arrange panel, and over MCP the forge_complete_stage answer plus forge_arrange. Nothing is arranged without the user's choice. The rules live in @radical/common (src/ai/forge/views.ts) and the placer in @radical/layout, for both.

ed9cf496-4559-4eed-bbac-8ba6d7d76300.description:
The model is only useful if it is consistent. When I drop a component on the bare canvas or connect two things our rules do not allow, the tool should refuse and tell me why instead of drawing it anyway. For a model I imported or whose rules I just changed, I want a list of everything that breaks the rules, so I can fix it.

I need the tool to know the C4 rules (what can sit inside what, which elements may be connected, how many of a type are allowed) and to refuse anything that breaks them with a message telling me why, instead of silently drawing something that is wrong. If my team uses its own metamodel, the same checks and the property forms should follow it.
Reconstructed from: manual#elements, manual#relations, manual#metamodel, manual#properties, landing (Metamodel 01, one validated graph). Merged on 2026-10-06 from the duplicate needs "Model that stays valid" and "Model stays valid".

f2d51835-1d89-4283-a8b9-6f3b3e060f05.description: Source, issues and pull requests (radicaltools/radical.tools). GitHub Actions: ci.yml runs on every pull request into main the workspace boundary check, type-check and tests (keeping a Vitest JSON report per workspace, artifact test-reports, via tools/test-reports.mjs), the E2E suite (unless labelled skip-e2e; report in e2e-report, with reports/e2e.json) and the MCP package check on Linux and Windows with Node 20 and 24. deploy.yml runs on every push to main: E2E first, then the checks and tests, then it builds Studio and the Hub and uploads them and the website to AWS through an OIDC role (no long-lived keys). release.yml drafts a GitHub Release with unsigned macOS, Windows and Linux installers on a v* tag that matches apps/studio/package.json (pull requests touching the packaging only build them); vscode-publish.yml publishes the VS Code extension on vscode-v* tags; the manual mcp-publish.yml verifies the npm tarball and, when not a dry run and on main, publishes that archive with npm Trusted Publishing and provenance. e2e-update-screenshots.yml regenerates the Linux screenshot baselines on a pull request labelled update-screenshots and commits them. CI does not run radical check: the architecture/ model is git-ignored.

f36ce8d2-42f3-4637-959d-43c6313d5af7.action: The canvas shall place every relation label at the middle of its path when that spot is free, and otherwise at the spot along or beside the path that covers the fewest element names, elements, other labels and relation lines, keeping labels off the ends of the path.
f36ce8d2-42f3-4637-959d-43c6313d5af7.label: Labels avoid overlaps
f36ce8d2-42f3-4637-959d-43c6313d5af7.precondition: a canvas has come to rest
f36ce8d2-42f3-4637-959d-43c6313d5af7.rationale: Each edge used to centre its label on its own path, so labels of parallel or crossing relations landed on each other and labels of short relations covered the elements they join. placeEdgeLabels places all labels of a canvas together, tries eleven spots along the path and two beside each, and weighs covering an element's name double. While the live layout moves elements, labels sit at the middle of their path and are placed again at rest. Evidence: packages/layout/src/edgeLabels.ts (placeEdgeLabels), packages/ui/src/components/edges/edgeGeometry.ts, packages/layout/tests/edgeLabels.test.ts, apps/e2e/tests/studio/edge-labels.spec.ts

fb78a7ee-a696-484c-a99f-c02525ed8b8e.alternatives: A transparent group (only the nearest ancestor that is not a group counts, by allowedParents alone): refuses a component in a group inside a system, which ADR Groups inside a system allows on purpose. A new field on a node type naming the ancestor it needs: one more thing to keep right in every preset, the metamodel editor and the file format, for a rule that follows from the fields already there. Leaving the rule and only hiding the types in the wiki: the canvas, the table and the MCP server would still allow it.
fb78a7ee-a696-484c-a99f-c02525ed8b8e.consequences: A group at the top of the model no longer takes containers, components, databases, web apps or queues; a group inside a system still does, so the shared packages of this model stay where they are. A group inside a system no longer takes a person, a domain, an entity or a blueprint. A model that already holds such an element keeps it and gets a warning in the Validation list (bad-place), not an error. None of the 260 bundled models and Hub concepts nor the sample holds one. Custom metamodels get the rule too, for their type with the id group.
fb78a7ee-a696-484c-a99f-c02525ed8b8e.context: Every C4 part lists the group among its allowed parents, so that a group can gather parts of a system (ADR Groups inside a system). The metamodel checked only the type of the direct parent, so a group gave a place to anything that names it: a component, container, database, web app or queue could be put into a group at the top of the model, where none of them may be, and a person or a domain into a group inside a system. Writing in the wiki made it one click: a new, empty group offered every such type.
fb78a7ee-a696-484c-a99f-c02525ed8b8e.decision: A group gives no place that an element could not have without it. A type that lists the group among its allowed parents may sit in a group only if the place where the group stands has room for it: at the top of the model, the types allowed at the root; under an element (the group's nearest ancestor that is not a group), the types that element can hold directly or deeper down by the allowed parents of the types in between. The rule is derived from allowedParents and allowedAtRoot, with no new field in the metamodel (isPlacementAllowed, hasPlaceUnder and placeOf in packages/common/src/metamodel/lookup.ts). It applies to adding, moving and retyping a node, to wrapping and unwrapping, and to moving a group, which is refused where what it holds would have no place. The wiki, the table, the selection bar and the Hub import offer only what the rule allows.
fb78a7ee-a696-484c-a99f-c02525ed8b8e.label: Groups hold what their place allows

Screenshot comparisons tolerate 0.5 % of pixels and run only on Linux (skipped elsewhere unless E2E_VISUAL=1); baselines come from the Playwright image and are regenerated by the update-screenshots label (e2e-update-screenshots.yml). .github/workflows/e2e.yml runs the suite inside mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble with two retries, called by ci.yml on every pull request (skipped with the skip-e2e label) and by deploy.yml before every deploy; it uploads the HTML report and reports/e2e.json, which radical check reads.

Threshold: npm run e2e passes in CI (two retries) with screenshot diffs under 0.5 % of pixels, before every deploy from main and on every pull request without the skip-e2e label.

fe6dd0dc-c792-4e57-b951-9f4e5468dce6.alternatives: A view kind 'report' in views.json: it would have to be created and saved in the model, and every model would need one; it may come later for slides that show a part of the report. A panel in Designer: too little room for the whole report. Calling the perspective Auditor, Reviewer, Verifier or Checker: the other perspectives name a role, Reviewer would clash with a review mode with comments, and Verifier with the verifies relation.
fe6dd0dc-c792-4e57-b951-9f4e5468dce6.consequences: Every model gets the report without setup and nothing is written into the model's files for it. Going to an element is one shared path (navigation.ts) for the Inspector and Quick Search. The Validation list in the metamodel editor still shows the metamodel issues on their own until it moves into the Inspector. Markers on the cards in Designer are a later step.
fe6dd0dc-c792-4e57-b951-9f4e5468dce6.context: radical check reports on the whole model (files, metamodel, completeness, what the tests say), but only as text in a terminal or CI log. The product owner wants the report in Studio, visual, with a link to every element it names. Studio already had four perspectives (Designer, Viewer, Presenter, the metamodel editor) and the Validation list, which shows the metamodel issues only.
fe6dd0dc-c792-4e57-b951-9f4e5468dce6.decision: Add a fifth perspective, Inspector, beside Designer, Viewer and Presenter. It shows the check of the open model as one page: summary tiles, errors with what they leave unverified, requirements by group, the elements that satisfy them, ADRs with their fitness functions, and every finding by rule. Each element it names is a link to a panel with its findings and tests, from which Studio shows it on a canvas or opens its wiki page. Like Viewer it edits nothing: leaving Designer parks the model and returning gives it back, and it takes no undo step. The toolbar button counts errors and warnings in every perspective and is greyed out while the model has no check report beside it.
fe6dd0dc-c792-4e57-b951-9f4e5468dce6.label: Inspector perspective
